clue.text: Game sometimes followed by Pass the Parcel?

definitions.text: Game sometimes followed by Pass the Parcel?

parts.words: Game sometimes followed by Pass the Parcel?
parts.note: a kissing party game named after the man who delivers the mail; after his rap at the door, a delivery man may well hand over a parcel, which is also the name of another party game

explanation.surface: A list of children's party games played one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a traditional party game in which kisses are exchanged at a pretend front door.

clue.text: Have power to remove a whole section of the orchestra?

definitions.meaning: to control events from behind the scenes, like a puppeteer working a marionette

definitions.text: remove a whole section of the orchestra?
definitions.meaning: taken literally, to take away every violin, viola, cello and double bass from the band

explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link between the two readings.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to control matters secretly, as a puppeteer works the cords of a puppet.

clue.text: Girl working in hairdressing establishment

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah
on means operating, as a machine that is switched on

explanation.surface: A young woman has a job at the hairdresser's.
explanation.definitionFit: A salon is a smart shop offering hairdressing or beauty treatments.

clue.text: End up imprisoning old women on one group of islands

indicators.note: imprisoning means holding something inside, so one piece is put within the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
crones are old women
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone ends up locking elderly ladies away on an island chain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the word for End, and 'on one' tacks I onto the old women before 'imprisoning' encloses them.
explanation.definitionFit: Micronesia is a region of many small Pacific islands, and also a nation made up of island groups.

clue.text: Principal features of mathematics book

definitions.meaning: the figures that arithmetic and maths chiefly deal with
the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.definitionFit: Figures are the stuff of mathematics, and this is also the title of a book of the Bible.

clue.text: Concerned with moving family and others round island

parts.note: kin means one's family or relations

indicators.note: round means the letters surround another piece

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and others
I is the abbreviation for island on maps

explanation.surface: Relatives and friends travel around an island together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the 'and others' abbreviation around the island letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic is a physics adjective meaning relating to motion.

clue.text: Our hall is regularly used for language exam

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Our hall is booked from time to time for a foreign-language test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of 'Our hall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test is a standard part of language examinations, where candidates must converse.

clue.text: Inject genetic material to cure criminal

indicators.note: to inject one thing into another is to put it inside, so these letters go within the second piece

parts.note: to kipper is to cure fish by salting and smoking
DNA is the molecule carrying genetic information

explanation.surface: A scientist proposes gene therapy as a medical remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cure' here is the food-preserving sense of smoking fish, not healing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abducts people for ransom is a criminal.

clue.text: Compose music for film, to pay off debts

parts.note: to compose oneself is to settle or calm down
the score is the music written for a film

explanation.surface: A composer writes a soundtrack to earn money owed to creditors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Compose' looks like writing music, but it is the calming sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to square an account, literally or in revenge, clearing what is owed.

clue.text: Shrub I planted between lakes round about

indicators.note: planted between means set in the middle of the two letters

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, so two lakes give two Ls

indicators.note: round means the word for about is turned backwards

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a bush between two lakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns the abbreviation for about backwards; 'planted between' sets I between the two lakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering shrub with fragrant purple or white blossom.

clue.text: Mistreat new worker engaged by fellow

indicators.note: engaged by means held inside, as a gear wheel is engaged

parts.note: a fellow is a male
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A recently hired labourer is taken on by a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fellow' gives the word for a man rather than a colleague; 'engaged by' sets the new worker inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To handle someone roughly is to mistreat them physically.

clue.text: Painter adding colour to old pot- tery, back in the centre

parts.note: a tint is a shade of colour

indicators.note: back means the word for earthenware is read backwards
in the centre means only the middle letters of the reversed word are kept

parts.note: taken as written: the hyphen is only the newspaper's line break

explanation.surface: An artist adds colour to an old ceramic piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of 'pottery' is OTTER, which 'back' turns into RETTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tintoretto was a sixteenth-century Venetian painter.

clue.text: Philosopher's hypocritical words, read aloud

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the philosopher is what follows

indicators.note: read aloud means the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk

explanation.surface: A thinker's pious statements are recited.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century German philosopher.

clue.text: Man without any money runs … to him?

definitions.text: Man without any money runs … to him?

parts.note: in chess, a pawn is a man or piece
broke means having no money
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A penniless man hurries to the person who lends on goods.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: someone broke runs to a lender on pledged goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A man who lends cash against pledged goods is where the penniless go.

clue.text: Train journalists no longer

parts.note: ex means former, no longer
the press means journalists collectively

explanation.surface: Trainee reporters are no longer in post.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a fast train that stops at few stations.

clue.text: Student of philosophy turned up a record: It's Not Unusual

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

indicators.note: unusual means the letters are rearranged into an unfamiliar order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A philosophy student spins a famous pop record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' gives PLA from A and LP; 'Unusual' rearranges ITSNOT into TONIST. 'It's Not Unusual' is a 1965 Tom Jones hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of Plato's philosophy is a student of philosophy.

clue.text: Place of worship shortly to be entered by religious man'

indicators.note: to be entered by means the next piece goes inside
shortly means cutting the last letter

parts.note: a chapel is a place of worship
pi is informal for pious, religious

explanation.surface: A church building receives a devout man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' drops the final L of the place of worship; 'to be entered by' sets the religious letters inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Chappie is informal British for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Sinatra performing for Russian noblewoman

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters acting out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra plays a Russian aristocrat on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsarina was the wife of a tsar, the Russian empress.

clue.text: A sign one is into current language

parts.note: the Ram is Aries, a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: is into means the letter is placed inside

parts.note: AC is alternating current
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A symbol is part of electrical current.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic is an ancient Semitic language.

clue.text: Butterfly one briefly spotted in early spring?

indicators.note: spotted in means seen inside

parts.note: March is a month of early spring

indicators.note: briefly means cutting a word's last letter

parts.note: one shortened gives the two letters ON

explanation.surface: A butterfly is first seen in early spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts the last letter from one; 'spotted in' places the result inside the month.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is a large orange and black butterfly.

clue.text: He's a saint, raising cap to the wife

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means reading upward, so backwards

parts.note: a tam is a Scottish cap
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gentleman lifts his hat to his wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Matthew was the apostle and gospel writer.

clue.text: Sprite's single trick

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': a sprite, a small screen graphic, is what follows

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a con is a trick

explanation.surface: A fairy plays a lone prank.
explanation.definitionFit: In computing a sprite is a small picture on screen, like a desktop symbol.

clue.text: Promotes early development 'of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held reads 'Promotes early development 'of' (4-6): it ends on a stray 'of', evidently cut short, with no wordplay for FASTTRACKS; a search of the text found nothing more.

clue.text: We've heard wrongdoer was mistaken for conspirator in Rome

indicators.note: we've heard means the word sounds like another

parts.note: a sinner is a wrongdoer

explanation.surface: A rumour that a criminal was mistaken for a conspirator.
explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar the poet Cinna was killed after being mistaken for Cinna the conspirator.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucius Cornelius Cinna was one of the plotters against Caesar.

clue.text: Adam, novel name for a venerable person?

definitions.meaning: George Eliot's novel Adam ... is titled with the surname
the Venerable ... was an Anglo-Saxon monk and historian

explanation.definitionFit: Eliot's hero is Adam Bede, and the Northumbrian monk is known as the Venerable Bede.

clue.text: Way before arriving at airport, first of passengers alighted in panic

indicators.note: in panic means the letters scramble
first of means taking the opening letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Air travellers spill out of the plane in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A glide path is the descending approach a plane follows before landing.

clue.text: Partly broken down fencing

indicators.note: Partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fence that is partly collapsed.
explanation.definitionFit: Kendo is Japanese sword fencing with bamboo staves.

clue.text: Into which France threw a rabble at the front?

definitions.text: Into which France threw a rabble at the front?

indicators.note: into which means the letters are made into the answer
at the front means taking the first letter

explanation.surface: France sends a mob into battle at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of FRANCE THREW A plus R (first of 'rabble') make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Front of the First World War was fought in trenches.
